A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShareLock framework and four-dataset visual generalization study. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial changes to the title, organization, settings, and experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original visual generalization, classification, retrieval, compositionality, and ablation results in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original visual generalization and ShareLock evaluations, including multilingual classification and new loss-function and backbone-scaling ablations.

M1.justification: V1's ViTeRB inherits ShareLock's architecture, whereas v2 explicitly uses a linear projection for strict zero-shot probing and a four-layer MLP for image-caption training (Sections 3.3 and 5.1). This changes the probing procedure while retaining ShareLock's frozen backbones, contrastive objective, and general-purpose MLP alignment.

E1.justification: V2 adds Chinese, Japanese, and Italian ImageNet evaluation (Table 3). Reported coverage loses ImageNet-V2, ObjectNet, quantitative Flickr8k/Flickr30k/MS-COCO retrieval, and SugarCrepe results. The four strict zero-shot datasets and image-caption training corpora remain; EuroSAT survives in appendix ablations.

E2.justification: V2 adds SLIP and LaCLIP to the CC3M and CC12M comparisons (Table 2). Visual-alignment comparisons also add CLIP's text encoder, ModernBERT, all-roberta-v1, and newer decoder-model families. CLIP, LiT, and ASIF remain; the retained DataComp-LAION rows are relabeled DataComp rather than constituting new comparators.

E3.justification: The default DINOv2 backbone changes from ViT-B/14 to ViT-L/14, although some appendix ablations retain the Base backbone. V2 separates linear probing from MLP-based caption alignment and replaces MMLU with MMLU-Pro for the correlation analysis. The strict seen/unseen class splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds SigLIP-versus-CLIP loss and Small-to-Giant DINOv2 scaling ablations (Appendix D), and revises the language- and vision-backbone comparisons. Projection-network analysis retains the earlier alternatives under revised names but drops retrieval and Winoground outcomes. The fine-tuning study is retained, moving from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 6.

E5.justification: V2 first specifies five initialization seeds and averaging visual-generalization results across them (Section 3.3 and Appendix E); v1 gives no corresponding training-run count. Correlation reporting changes from R-squared to Pearson coefficients. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or dispersion estimates, and the new disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: ShareLock's reported CC3M/CC12M ImageNet accuracies change from 52.1%/59.1% to 54.5%/62.0%, alongside the backbone revision, so these are not established same-setting gains. V2 adds multilingual and dataset-level language-model results, revises rankings and ablation outcomes, and removes extensive retrieval and SugarCrepe scores. Its MMLU-Pro Pearson coefficients are different statistics under different conditions from v1's MMLU results.

T1.justification: The disjoint-class condition, contrastive-loss mathematics, cosine similarity, and classification rule are retained. V2's omission of an image-side projection from the notation matches v1's stated implementation without image transformations. Neither version contains substantive theoretical proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: V2 makes cross-lingual transfer a central abstract, introduction, and conclusion claim, prominently reporting Chinese classification performance. It also positions the contribution as the first direct analysis of intrinsic visual alignment, shifting emphasis from the named ViTeRB benchmark and ShareLock's training-efficiency headline. The underlying decoder-alignment and data-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit caveats about confounding architecture with pretraining data, objectives, and parameter count, plus LLM forward-pass costs and limited training scale. It introduces multilingual-transfer explanations and suggests unchanged vision representations can limit compositionality. Conversely, v1's detailed retrieval-weakness discussion and NV-Embed-based remedy are removed.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 provides a project-page link and states that code and models are published, although Appendix A retains future-tense wording. V2 separately documents the probing recipe, including cosine scheduling and a 3.5k-step maximum, while omitting v1's explicit Batch Normalization detail. Resource availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the broad data-efficient CLIP discussion with positioning around vision-language alignment, including new comparisons to Maniparambil et al. and Zhang et al. V2 adds concept-leakage and architectural-limitation references, including Xu et al., Mayilvahanan et al., and Jose et al., while removing much of the data-filtering literature discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, and much of the experimental narrative are rewritten. Method and probing material are reorganized into Section 3, ViTeRB terminology is removed, fine-tuning analysis moves to the appendix, and the appendices become separate thematic sections. This is extensive restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the model schematic, revises the correlation plots, merges the main classification tables, and adds multilingual and ablation tables. Several extended benchmark tables disappear, while fine-tuning and feature-extraction displays move to the appendix. The qualitative retrieval image panels are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence with broader language-model comparisons, multilingual tests, new ablations, five-seed reporting, and clearer confounding limitations. However, removing v1's quantitative retrieval comparisons and associated failure discussion reduces transparency. New reporting errors also remain: Section 5.2 labels Table 3's Japanese scores as Italian, and Section 4 reverses the Llama-3/NV-Embed numerical attributions. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
